title: Coins are reset: prices sit on the coin curves
summary: The coin reset is in the game's data. Shop Tokens, Guild Hall ranks and the first ring of places ask coins sized by the coin rule, and enemies and Hideout thefts pay about half a worker. Leaving the Starter Camp now takes about 41 minutes for one hero (it was 14), when the hero is level 10 or 11. The owner ruled that the three rings arrive at about level 10, 30 and 50; the places are being re-placed before rings 2 and 3 are priced.
checked: After the coin reset, 2026-11-27 (workspace revision 107): all 115 coin prices are within the tolerance of the coin curve. The way out of the Starter Camp comes at 41 minutes against 35 (19 % over, inside the 25 %); Plane 1's at 1 h 12 against 1 h 44 and Plane 2's at 3 h 33 against 3 h 50, both waiting on rings 2 and 3. A worker sells about 3,600 coins an hour in the Starter Camp, 4,100 in Plane 1, 9,400 in Plane 2 and 16,000 to 54,000 in Plane 3; Goblin thefts fell from 6,350 an hour to about 1,800.

Days to 99 for a maxed hero against 12.65, same date: Smithing 12.6, Cooking 12.8, Mining 14.2, Alchemy 14.4, Farming 15.3, Construction 15.8, Crafting 16.1, Forestry 21.2, Fishing 23.8. Fishing and Forestry are the two still far off. The ledger counts 692 warnings (734 before the three packs).

The Starter Camp's coin curve gives two answers by turns, because what a hero sells there depends on which Guild Hall ranks the reference guild can afford. The pack took numbers inside the tolerance of both (250, 1,500 and 2,100).

Round 2, 2026-11-27, on the owner's recalculated workspace (revision 97). Days to 99 for a maxed hero, before and after the XP corrections, against 12.65: Smithing 22.4 to 12.6, Cooking 19.6 to 12.8, Mining 24.0 to 14.2, Alchemy 20.5 to 14.6, Farming 23.2 to 15.4, Construction 19.5 to 15.8, Crafting 31.1 to 16.1, Forestry 39.8 to 21.2, Fishing 23.8 unchanged. From level 40 up Mining, Forestry, Farming, Cooking, Crafting and Smithing sit within 5 % of the curve to the end of their content. Warnings fall from 734 to 717.

The three-pack trial, 2026-11-27. Days to 99 for a maxed hero against the curve's 12.6: with no packs 2.4 to 8.4 (far too fast); with the number pack and the boosts pack 19.5 to 39.8 (too slow, because the live game holds fewer boosts than the XP assumes); with the ledger's 66 XP corrections on top: Smithing 12.4, Cooking 12.8, Alchemy 14.2, Mining 14.2, Farming 15.4, Construction 15.8, Crafting 16.0, Forestry 20.8, Fishing 23.8. Within the levels each skill's content covers, pace is 0.96 to 1.07 of the curve for Forestry, Mining, Farming, Crafting and Cooking; Smithing 0.78 to 1.10; Alchemy and Construction run fast early (0.56 to 0.75). The days figures run higher than that because several skills have nothing past level 80 to 90.

Still off after the three packs: Fishing (too fast to 60, too slow after); a typical hero is 1.6 to 1.8 times behind a maxed one in Cooking and Alchemy, over the 1.45 bound; the first place still asks level 5, so the Starter Camp's way out is 13 minutes; 76 live entries got no numbers.

The ledger now counts heroes (one at the start, eight at the end), spends each hour of work once and times a work site by its building places. With one hero, everything the Starter Camp offers today takes about 7 hours: nine skills and its prices, about 15 hours of work in all. That is information, not a fault, by the ruling on leaving a stage; it is a lot for a first camp.

The ledger's reading of the live game, 2026-11-26 (the 6.25 % curve, a maker held to about 2 gatherers, the new boost budget). Days to 99 for a maxed hero against the curve's 12.6: Cooking 3.8, Alchemy 5.3, Farming 6.6, Forestry 6.8, Construction 7.3, Smithing 7.6, Crafting 9.1, Mining 9.5, Fishing 21.7. So before any number pack the live game is mostly 1.3 to 3.3 times too fast, Cooking most of all, and Fishing is well too slow (it moved from 14.7 with the day's content changes).

Boosts in the live game: 462 pieces of work hold more boost than their tier's budget (it was 883 before the typical player's budget rose to three quarters), most of them speed from station upgrades. A typical hero falls more than 1.45 times behind the curve in Fishing, Farming 20 to 30 and early Forestry.
Three walls, where a stretch takes over twice the curve's time; eighteen chains need more than about 2 gatherers a maker to run in full.

The page and the ledger still time different content: the plan isn't in the CMS. The ledger's method now matches the rules on the curve, the chain and the budget; it does not yet count heroes by tier or stacked buildings (T-716).
Pace, all twelve skills: no level is slower than 1.3x the curve. The slowest is the end of Forestry's run from 81 to 98.
Empty stretches: 33 flagged. 15 last more than a day of typical play and are on the gaps list; 2 in Construction wait on its repeatable work; the rest last minutes or hours and are left alone.

Fishing: most of its old stretches were the page's mistake. It didn't count a catch with its own level (Salmon at 40, Lobster at 50, Swordfish at 63) as something new. Fishing now has 17 unlocks, not 8, and Cooked Salmon no longer shows as arriving at the start of the game.
Cooking and Smithing (first run, same day): on the curve, no empty stretches, every new recipe pays more than the one before.

The method itself, with two read-only readings of the CMS's simulator and ledger: docs/active/balance_method_review.md. The page is on the curve by construction (XP is worked back from the curve), so it cannot test whether a guild's set-up is realistic; only the ledger or play can.
moved: Synced by the owner, 2026-11-27: the coin reset pack, 71 entries. Five Shop Tokens 420 to 250 coins; every Guild Hall rank to 1,500, 3,000, 9,100 or 19,000 by its stage; settling a place in ring 1 420 to 2,100; coins a kill on all 25 enemies at half a worker's rate (Goblin 28 to 15, bosses 170 to 390, Troll 1,400); coins a theft on three camps (Goblin 28 to 8).

Ruled by the owner, 2026-11-27: the three rings arrive at about level 10, 30 and 50 (about 40 minutes, 4 hours and 15 hours in), each asking a level a few below the target and a coin price, so a guild that sells well arrives a little sooner. The iron-age places move into ring 1, ring 2 holds silver and gold, ring 3 mythril onward. This replaces the ruling of rings asking level 10 and 20, which measured at 65 minutes for the Starter Camp.

Ruled by the owner, 2026-11-27: a rare drop is worth more in proportion to its rarity, not squared (a Bird Nest fell from 85 coins to 23), and a lone hero making slowly in the first levels is accepted.
Synced by the owner, 2026-11-27: the XP corrections pack (64 values), the Bird Nest packs from the content session, and the rare-drop worths.

Staged with the owner's yes, 2026-11-27: the XP corrections pack, 64 XP values. Five early recipes were held back from the tool's 66: Copper Ingot and Shrimp unchanged, Charcoal 5, Elixir of Ironskin 9, Birdwatcher 8. Raised as the tool proposed, each became the best XP in its skill until about level 40, because the next station runs the same recipe about 1.7 times faster.

What the page learned: a correction may not make a work out-pay, at any later level, the work that was best there before. Early levels that only a starter recipe covers are a gap for content, not an XP raise.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-27: XP follows the boosts that exist. Numbers reach the game as the number pack, the boosts pack, then the ledger's XP corrections on top; as content adds boosts, the corrections are re-run and XP comes down toward the rule's figure.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-26: gear is for combat, not work, and tools gate work without speeding it, so neither has a share of the work budget; skill perks may give speed or yield but not XP, because a player doesn't choose their perks.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-26: a hero has one drink active, and drinks, potions and elixirs all count as drinks; one boost item of another type (such as a scroll, not designed yet) may be held beside it. Poisons, bait, arrows and Motes are not boosts and are not limited. The game allows more than this today, so it is a game change (T-738).
Approved by the owner, 2026-11-26: the first number pack waits for a boosts pack and they land together, followed by one coin reset.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-26, the boost budget counting only what a hero can hold at once: four Faster Work buildings or station upgrade steps at 5 % each, skill perks 15 %, Guild Hall stars 10 % (small steps), and one consumable in all, a speed drink at 15 %: 60 % off work time late in the game, the same total as before. XP: four More XP buildings at 2.5 % and Hall stars 10 %. Yield: Double Output buildings at +50 % each, up to four.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-26, replacing the 30 seconds ruled the day before: a node gives about 15 seconds of work and is back in about a minute, so a hero needs 4 or 5 nodes to stay busy. A gathering site then has about 5 places left for buildings.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-26: leaving a stage means settling the next place (level 10 in one or two skills and its price, about 35 minutes for the Starter Camp), not finishing everything the stage offers.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-26, after spacing was settled (reach 240, Tokens 128 apart, 12 places round a node, about 8 for buildings): the same building all game and more of them. A Faster Work building is 5 % off work time, one held at copper and four at darkmetal; a More XP building is +2.5 % XP; a Double Output building +25 % yield.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-26: a typical player holds three quarters of each boost, not half. The typical line on this page moves from about 23 days a skill to about 17.5, and typical ends about 1.4 times behind optimized, not 2 times.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-26: worth follows the XP rule (an hour of work is worth twice as much every 20 levels, not the simulator's 260-fold rise), and a well-run guild is comfortable for coins.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-26: boosts are placed and a site must choose. With Tokens edges touching and reach unchanged (the owner's leaning), a node has about 8 places for buildings, about 4 of them max one kind of boost, and a typical player fills most places. A station's own upgrade counts as a boost.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-26: drinks and work potions last 25 work cycles, 5 a craft, at twice the strength (this replaces yesterday's 50 cycles). The extra comes from the buildings' share: about 5 % a building for speed.
Approved by the owner, 2026-11-26: the Starter Camp ends at level 10, 35 minutes in on the curve; a skilled player leaves in about 20.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-26, from a challenge of the method: the pace curve describes a hero who splits time between training and supplying the guild; heroes arrive about one a tier; two or three heroes share each job; a new hero starts at about half the guild's level through XP for Everyone.

Found, not yet fixed: the boost budget counts one of each building, but stacking buildings on a node is intended and today's spacing lets 30 Tokens stand in reach of one node. The owner wants spacing and reach settled first, with at most 12 in a radius (T-718). Until then the page's optimized and typical lines are estimates.

Found, not yet fixed: early arrivals on this page assume a full chain from the first minute. With one hero, Smithing 1 to 19 is about 7 hours of chain work, not 1.7; with two at iron, 20 to 29 is 4.8 hours, not 2.1.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-25, the reference guild: 8 heroes running a few supply chains at a time, about 2 gatherers per maker at every tier. A lone hero at one node is busy half the time and a node is back in about 30 seconds; a camp with two nodes keeps a gatherer fully busy.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-25: one total reward an hour, tilted by purpose. Training work pays 1.5x the XP and half the goods, earning work half the XP and 1.5x the goods. The plan's entries aren't tagged yet, so the page treats all of them as balanced.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-25: the balance rules are the one rulebook; a typical player is one who buys what pays back soon; and the pace of one skill for one hero governs, so every skill at 99 on all 8 heroes is a one to two year goal.
Corrected: the page's typical line is a planning estimate (half of every boost). The engine's definition applies once the content is in the CMS.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-25, the coin rule: an item's worth is the time in it; an everyday purchase's coins cost one level's time of one hero's selling (5 minutes at copper, 6 hours at darkmetal) and a big one (a new place, a Hall star) half its item price's work (30 minutes at copper, 12 hours at darkmetal); a fighter earns about half a worker's coins; the coin building adds at most 10 %.

Approved by the owner, 2026-11-25: the pace step's range is 6 % to 6.5 % a level, to tighten the late game; the page uses 6.25 %, the middle, until the boosts are balanced. Level 98 takes 18 hours instead of 22.5, levels 81 to 98 take 8.4 days optimized and 16 typical (were 10 and 20), and levels 1 to 60 barely change.
Approved by the owner, 2026-11-25: a gap for content is a stretch of more than a day of typical play with nothing new.
Approved by the owner, 2026-11-25: the optimized player's boosts climb level by level between tiers, so a new tier's first recipes never pay less than the old tier's last.
Approved by the owner, 2026-11-25: gear takes 50 % longer for each bar past the first. A Chestplate takes 3x a Dagger.
Approved by the owner, 2026-11-25: a recipe with a made base takes 1 of each raw ingredient at every level.
Approved by the owner, 2026-11-25: a Fletching craft makes 40 arrows; a bar makes 40 Arrowheads or 40 Kunai, or 5 Nails.
Approved by the owner, 2026-11-25: a drink lasts 50 work cycles and a craft makes 5.

Fixed: a Token no longer moves off the level of what it gives, and a catch stays on the level of the recipe that uses it. The page had moved the Oyster Bed, the Clay Deposit, the Hollow Tree and Seaweed away from their items. 12 unlocks still move, each by 3 levels, to break up a thin stretch.
Fixed earlier today: food costed like armour, Water counts, unlocks moving below an ingredient, and action lengths trimmed so whole XP pays exactly.
proposals: Held for the next pack, not yet put to the owner: four small XP raises the corrections tool now proposes (Birdwatcher 8 to 13, Elixir of Ironskin 9 to 12, Iron Dagger 8 to 11, Iron Wand 13 to 18). They go with the ring pack.
For the next pack: ring 2 and ring 3 levels and coins, and the stage time targets, once the places are re-placed.
gaps: New, 2026-11-27: with the rings at about level 10, 30 and 50, the places need re-placing between rings (iron age into ring 1, silver and gold in ring 2, mythril onward in ring 3). It is the first entry in docs/active/balance_gaps.md, for the content session.
The first 15 levels of Smithing, Crafting and Alchemy run slow with one hero. The owner accepted it: nothing to fill.

15 stretches are open for the content session, in docs/active/balance_gaps.md. The longest: Forestry 81 to 98 (17 days typical on Ebony alone), Fletching 86 to 98 and Crafting 87 to 98 (13 days each), Farming 88 to 98 (12 days).
Nine of the fifteen are a skill's last run to 99. Smithing and Cooking don't have one, because they have something new at 98 and 99.
waiting: On the content session: re-place the places between the three rings (a change pack for the owner).
On the balancer, after that: one pack for ring 2 and 3 levels, their coins and the stage time targets, with the four small XP raises.

On the owner, later: whether a typical player re-judges drinks as the guild grows and how the typical player buys Guild Hall ranks; three rules still to set (cycles a summon lasts, crop growing time, how far apart chains of one tier may pay).
On the balancer: Fishing and Forestry pace, and Steady Stills rank 1, which now pays back in about 5 hours against a 2-hour target.
On the content session: the fifteen long stretches; 76 live entries that got no numbers; late-game yield beyond buildings.
